comparisons.judgment: Adaptive exact counting and the iterated counting hierarchy expose distinct broad questions about PSPACE and closure. Exact-normalizer collapses remain genuine lost targets, not aliases; under breadth the counting-level pair is preferred.

Parallel versus adaptive NP queries supplies a different resource axis with natural complete problems. FewP=UP is the cleanest zero-credit casualty and the most reasonable contrary preference; positive residual score alone does not settle the comparison.

Logspace quantum computation and logspace majority/linear algebra add new resource comparisons. Keeping the opposite randomized or unambiguous polarity would restore real asymmetric interfaces, but with greater overlap in the already represented polynomial-time family.

Uniform NC1 versus L is an additional central parallelism question. PH and Sigma2P preserve broad second-level collapse/separation consequences, although Pi2P-specific points and independence do not transfer automatically.

Unentangled quantum proofs, constrained nonnegative quantum verification, and quantum statistical zero knowledge introduce different verification resources. They must compete under the same total-language restriction, not receive a bonus for quantum terminology. Complement closure headlines still have scored consequences; asymmetric UP/FewP interfaces are lost.

Retains nondeterministic linear-exponential/spectrum interfaces and explicit exponential time-space gaps. E supplies finer deterministic resource questions and remains a defensible restoration for a different emphasis; its current ordinary hypotheses all retain some scored consequence.

selection_sanity_check.counterargument: A benchmark emphasizing structural refinements over family breadth should restore FewP and potentially LWPP/WPP or coUP, even at the expense of one or more new endpoint slots. The present choice is not justified by claiming their lost results are unimportant.
